0b148d64.candidate_factory_source:
"""Odd-quadrant crop (0b148d64), reviewed for the broader RE-ARC domain.

Rule (native constructor and RE-ARC ``generate_0b148d64``): background bands
split the grid into four quadrants. Three are drawn in one colour and one in
another; the output crops the odd quadrant.

The earlier factory fixed the background to palette[0] and selected the
rarest foreground colour. RE-ARC samples the background and the quadrant
densities, so neither assumption holds there. This program uses the
geometric property that both constructors share. The odd colour lies inside
one quadrant, the shared colour spans three quadrants (so both band
directions), and the background bands span the grid. The odd colour is
therefore the colour with the strictly smallest bounding box (RE-ARC's own
verifier rule), and the output is that bounding box. In the native domain,
this is the same quadrant the rarest-colour rule chose. No colour or
orientation constant is needed.
"""

PROGRAM = r'''
def solve(demonstrations, grid):
    boxes = {}
    for row, cells in enumerate(grid):
        for col, colour in enumerate(cells):
            top, left, bottom, right = boxes.get(colour, (row, col, row, col))
            boxes[colour] = (min(top, row), min(left, col), max(bottom, row), max(right, col))
    if len(boxes) < 3:
        raise ValueError("Expected a background and two quadrant colours")
    ranked = sorted(((bottom - top + 1) * (right - left + 1), colour)
                    for colour, (top, left, bottom, right) in boxes.items())
    if ranked[0][0] == ranked[1][0]:
        raise ValueError("Ambiguous odd quadrant: equal bounding-box areas")
    top, left, bottom, right = boxes[ranked[0][1]]
    return [row[left:right + 1] for row in grid[top:bottom + 1]]
'''


def build_program(d4, palette):
    # Bounding-box areas are invariant under D4 and colour permutation.
    return PROGRAM

1b2d62fb.candidate_rule: Divider = centre line of an odd dimension in one non-background colour, either axis (RE-ARC transposes half its scenes); background 0 and marker 8 stay palette roles. Exact on 300/300 raw RE-ARC pairs under all 8 D4 maps (archived verifier agreed on 142/300) and 150/150 native augmented episodes.
1b2d62fb.candidate_factory_source:
"""Shared-empty-cell overlay (1b2d62fb), reviewed for the broader RE-ARC domain.

Rule (native constructor and RE-ARC ``generate_1b2d62fb``): a one-cell divider
splits the grid into two equal halves. An output cell is the marker colour
where both halves are background, and background elsewhere.

Both constructors fix the background (0) and marker (8) colours, so those
remain palette roles. The earlier factory also fixed the divider colour to
palette[1] and its axis to the D4 index. RE-ARC samples the divider and
half colours and transposes half of its scenes, so this program finds the
divider instead. It is the centre line of an odd dimension, in one non-
background colour. Halves cannot form such a line in the other axis,
because a crossing line would contain the divider cell and half cells of other colours.
A missing or doubly-possible divider is rejected.
"""


def build_program(d4, palette):
    background = int(palette[0])
    marker = int(palette[8])
    return '''
BACKGROUND = %d
MARKER = %d


def solve(demonstrations, grid):
    height, width = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    centre_col = [row[width // 2] for row in grid] if width %% 2 else None
    centre_row = grid[height // 2] if height %% 2 else None
    vertical = bool(centre_col) and len(set(centre_col)) == 1 and centre_col[0] != BACKGROUND
    horizontal = bool(centre_row) and len(set(centre_row)) == 1 and centre_row[0] != BACKGROUND
    if vertical == horizontal:
        raise ValueError("Expected exactly one central divider line")
    if vertical:
        half = width // 2
        first = [row[:half] for row in grid]
        second = [row[half + 1:] for row in grid]
    else:
        half = height // 2
        first = grid[:half]
        second = grid[half + 1:]
    return [[MARKER if a == BACKGROUND and b == BACKGROUND else BACKGROUND
             for a, b in zip(row_a, row_b)] for row_a, row_b in zip(first, second)]
''' % (background, marker)
